mcp_dispatch.source: python -m pip download mcp==1.28.0 --no-deps -d <scratch>/mcp (Windows Python 3.14); the wheel mcp-1.28.0-py3-none-any.whl was unzipped in scratch and the FastMCP files read there; nothing was installed into the repository
mcp_dispatch.rule: In mcp 1.28.0 FastMCP, Tool.run awaits FuncMetadata.call_fn_with_arg_validation, which for a plain def (is_async False) calls fn(**arguments) directly inside the coroutine with no thread hop, so a sync @mcp.tool body runs on the event loop thread and blocks it for the call. The FastMCP tool path has no anyio.to_thread or run_in_executor (tool_manager.py, server.py, base.py and func_metadata.py were each read for one). Only an async def tool body is awaited on the loop; a sync one is not.
evidence: mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py:93-96 (if fn_is_async: await fn(...); else: return fn(**...) with no thread)
mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:343-346 (async call_tool awaits the tool manager; no thread)

lake.method: boto3 1.43.114 (scratch venv) list_objects_v2 paginated with Prefix audit/dt=<day>/ for each of the 7 UTC days, every key counted (the window ends on today's UTC date, which is the 7th day); then get_object on every 6-th key of the sorted key list (11441 objects; up to 3 retries after the first try, zero failed); each body is one JSON line, counted by its tool key or, when absent, its event key. Only names and counts were kept; no principal, email, account or token value was copied, printed or stored.

ranking.proposal: Bound the audit-lake write in audit._emit: give the boto3 client at audit.py:55 a botocore Config with connect and read timeouts and a retry cap, so one slow put cannot hold a request for an unbounded time; no thread or queue change.
ranking.basis: all 81 sites reach audit._emit (audit.py:40), the single writer; audit.py sets no timeout today; the 7-day volume is 68646 scaled writes at k=6; 80 of 81 sites are on the loop, so the bound covers the blocking case on every one of them

ranking.proposal: Move the S3 put off the event loop: run audit._emit's boto3 leg through anyio.to_thread.run_sync, or a single background writer with a bounded queue, so the on-loop sites do not wait on put_object; the local file append stays inline.
ranking.basis: 80 of 81 sites are on the loop (mcp 1.28.0 sync-tool rule); 68646 scaled writes in 7 days is about 9806 per day or 6.8 per minute, so the loop wait is paid per call and a thread hop removes it

ranking.proposal: Batch the Teams read audit: hx_teams writes one record per call and is the largest name in the lake, so one aggregated record per poll would cut the volume without touching the tools' answers.
ranking.basis: per_tool_counts hx_teams 25410 scaled of 68646 (37.0 percent); the literal site is teams_route.py:172 only, the other large names are reached through the shared _run chokepoint and have no literal site

ranking.proposal: Make no repair yet: measure the put_object latency from the gateway to the lake before choosing a change, since the lake write is best-effort and this cell measured counts, not wait time.
ranking.basis: the per-site counts size the volume only; no put latency was measured by this cell, so the wait cannot be sized from the table
